<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4` fails to start on gfx942 (MI300X/MI325X). This PR runs its routed experts there on the existing AITER Triton W4A16 kernels, keeping the MXFP4 weights and using BF16 activations. Changes are confined to the Muse Spark AMD MoE runner, its tests, and the Muse Spark recipe.

## Claims

- The Quark MXFP4 checkpoint now serves on gfx942 with TP: GSM8K 96.97% on 4x MI325X (TP4), where it previously failed at model construction.
- DFlash2 speculative decoding works on top of it unchanged (acceptance length 4.96 on GSM8K with `RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2`).
- gfx950 behaviour is unchanged: the CK W4A4 experts are still selected whenever the oracle picks `AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4`.

## Validation

**Reproducer (before).** On 4x MI325X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (`0.32.1rc1.dev602+g5d35ce393`, same `muse_moe_runner.py` as main):

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --language-model-only --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --max-model-len 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --reasoning-parser muse
```

```
NotImplementedError: MuseSpark1x MXFP4 on ROCm requires the AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4 backend; got EMULATION.
```

**After**, same command with this PR's `muse_moe_runner.py` mounted into the image. These end-to-end runs predate the rebase; the runner is unchanged by it, and the rebase only adapted the test to main's `triton_weight()` storage (#62407). CUDA graphs on (the engine resolves to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`), greedy, max 4096 output tokens, concurrency 64, `--speculative-config '{"method": "dflash", "model": <draft>, "num_speculative_tokens": 7}'`:

| Draft | GSM8K acc (1319) | GSM8K AL | GSM8K output tok/s | SPEED-Bench qualitative AL (mean of 11 categories) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `RadixArk/Muse-Spark-Open-DFlash2` | 96.97% | 4.96 | 1,663 | 3.96 |
| `nvidia/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-DFlash2` | 96.59% | 4.55 | 1,521 | 3.78 |

The NVIDIA draft's SPEED-Bench AL is in line with its model card (3.84 greedy, NVFP4 target on GB300). One run each; the two servers ran on separate 4-GPU halves of the node, partly concurrently, so throughput is indicative only.

**Unit tests**, MI325X, rebased on main (`5689c2790c`), run in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` `0.33.0rc1.dev484+g76c6f3f2a` with this PR's files and main's `amd/model.py` mounted, `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_muse_spark_rocm_bf16_moe.py`: 32 passed, 3 skipped (gfx950-only).

- `test_rocm_aiter_w4a16_mxfp4_moe_matches_dequantized_reference` (gfx942) builds a real `RoutedExperts` and `MuseSparkQuarkOCPMXFusedMoE`, loads MXFP4 weights through `process_weights_after_loading`, and runs the resulting kernel against an explicit reference on the dequantized weights, including the post-expert norm and router weighting. It covers 16 routes (aiter's fused sort), 64 routes, and 65,544 routes (int32 indices), and checks that CUDA graph replay matches eager exactly. With the gate/up interleave removed, all three cases fail (~97% of elements mismatched).
- `test_muse_mxfp4_method_requires_w4a4_aiter` also covers the gfx942 selection and checks that an explicit `--moe-backend` is not replaced.

`pre-commit run` on the changed files passes, and the recipe validates with `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm` from vllm-project/recipes.

**CI.** The `(MI300) MoE Kernels` step runs `tests/kernels/moe` on gfx942, so the new test runs there. The gfx942 end-to-end run needs the 509 GB checkpoint and is not in CI; it was run locally as above.

## Details

**Root cause.** The Muse Spark ROCm MoE accepts only the CK W4A4 experts (`AITER_MXFP4_MXFP4`), which need gfx950's FP4 matrix cores. On gfx942 the Quark W4A4 oracle falls back to `EMULATION`, which the model rejects.

**Fix.**

- On gfx942 with AITER enabled and `--moe-backend` `auto`/`aiter`/`aiter_triton_mxfp4_bf16`, `MuseSparkQuarkOCPMXFusedMoE` switches to `AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_BF16` with the new `MuseSparkAiterW4A16Experts`. Other cases raise as before.
- `MuseSparkAiterW4A16Experts` keeps the route-preserving contract of the CK experts. Each expanded (token, route) row is routed top-1 by a one-hot logit, so the softmax gate is exactly 1 and GEMM2 writes one unweighted output per route. That output goes to the existing `MuseSparkTopKWeightAndReduce` (post-expert norm, router weights, TP reduction). The stock `aiter_triton_kernel_w4a16_moe_forward` does the work; no new kernels.
- The Triton SwiGLU epilogue reads gate/up as interleaved row pairs while Muse loads `w13` as `[gate | up]`, so `process_weights_after_loading` interleaves the `w13` rows and scales before Quark's Triton swizzle.
- `AITER_TRITON_USE_HERD` changes aiter's top-k selection and could drop the one-hot expert, so the new experts reject it.

**Limitations.**

- TP only; expert parallelism is rejected on this path.
- Numerics differ from gfx950 because activations stay BF16 instead of dynamic MXFP4.
- The BF16 -> MXFP4 online path (`VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_ONLINE_QUANT=mxfp4`) goes through the same code but was not run end to end on gfx942.
- The recipe's AMD flags (`ROCM_AITER_FA`, breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs, TP8) were not validated on gfx942, so the recipe documents gfx942 support in its guide without adding MI300X/MI325X to `supported_hardware`.
- No throughput comparison against the BF16 checkpoint or FP8 requantization.

**Not a duplicate.** Open Muse Spark AMD PRs either speed up the gfx950 MXFP4 path (#63290, #63263, #63298, #63254) or target the separate PTPC-FP8 checkpoint on MI300X (#63721–#63725, #63727, #63729). None enables the MXFP4 checkpoint on gfx942. Several touch `muse_moe_runner.py`, but not the backend selection.

**AI assistance.** This PR was written with AI assistance (Codex with Claude Opus 5.5; review by a separate Claude Opus 5.5 agent). I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and evaluations above.

---

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

     ROCM_AITER_SUPPORTED = is_aiter_found_and_supported()
 
@@ -557,6 +577,138 @@ def _mxfp4_weights(
     return w13_quant, w2_quant, quant_config
 
 
+_E2M1_VALUES = (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0)
+
+
+def _dequant_mxfp4(packed: torch.Tensor, scales: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Reference OCP MXFP4 dequant: low nibble first, e8m0 scale per 32."""
+    magnitudes = torch.tensor(_E2M1_VALUES, device=packed.device)
+    lut = torch.cat((magnitudes, -magnitudes))
+    values = torch.stack(
+        (lut[(packed & 0xF).long()], lut[(packed >> 4).long()]), dim=-1
+    ).flatten(-2)
+    block_scales = torch.exp2(scales.view(torch.uint8).float() - 127.0)
+    return (values.unflatten(-1, (-1, 32)) * block_scales[..., None]).flatten(-2)
+
+
+def _reference_route_outputs(
+    hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    w13: torch.Tensor,
+    w2: torch.Tensor,
+    topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Unweighted SiLU-gated expert output per route; w13 rows are [gate | up]."""
+    num_tokens, top_k = topk_ids.shape
+    intermediate_size = w2.shape[-1]
+    rows = hidden_states.repeat_interleave(top_k, dim=0)
+    expert_ids = topk_ids.reshape(-1)
+    out = torch.empty_like(rows)
+    for expert in range(w13.shape[0]):
+        idx = (expert_ids == expert).nonzero().squeeze(1)
+        gate_up = (rows[idx].float() @ w13[expert].float().T).to(rows.dtype)
+        gate, up = gate_up.split(intermediate_size, dim=-1)
+        activated = (torch.nn.functional.silu(gate.float()) * up.float()).to(rows.dtype)
+        out[idx] = (activated.float() @ w2[expert].float().T).to(rows.dtype)
+    return out.view(num_tokens, top_k, -1)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not ROCM_GFX942, reason="requires a GFX942 GPU")
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not ROCM_AITER_SUPPORTED, reason="requires supported AITER")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_tokens,top_k",
+    # 16 routes take aiter's fused sort, 65,544 routes its int32 indices.
+    [(2, 8), (16, 4), (8193, 8)],
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_rocm_aiter_w4a16_mxfp4_moe_matches_dequantized_reference(
+    enable_rocm_aiter,
+    default_vllm_config,
+    dist_init,
+    workspace_init,
+    num_tokens: int,
+    top_k: int,
+) -> None:
+    torch.manual_seed(1234)
+    num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size = 8, 256, 256
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    default_vllm_config.model_config = ModelConfig()
+    with device:
+        layer = FusedMoEFactory(
+            num_experts=num_experts,
+            top_k=top_k,
+            hidden_size=hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=intermediate_size,
+            prefix="experts",
+        ).routed_experts
+    method = MuseSparkQuarkOCPMXFusedMoE(layer.moe_config, kMxfp4Static, kMxfp4Dynamic)
+    assert method.mxfp4_backend is Mxfp4MoeBackend.AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_BF16
+
+    w13_packed, w13_scales = _quantize_experts_to_mxfp4(
+        torch.randn(
+            num_experts, 2 * intermediate_size, hidden_size, dtype=dtype, device=device
+        )
+        / hidden_size**0.5
+    )
+    w2_packed, w2_scales = _quantize_experts_to_mxfp4(
+        torch.randn(
+            num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, dtype=dtype, device=device
+        )
+        / intermediate_size**0.5
+    )
+    w13_ref = _dequant_mxfp4(w13_packed, w13_scales).to(dtype)
+    w2_ref = _dequant_mxfp4(w2_packed, w2_scales).to(dtype)
+
+    with device:
+        method.create_weights(layer, num_experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, dtype)
+    layer.w13_weight.copy_(w13_packed)
+    layer.w2_weight.copy_(w2_packed)
+    layer.w13_weight_scale.copy_(w13_scales)
+    layer.w2_weight_scale.copy_(w2_scales)
+    layer.post_expert_norm_fn = _rms_norm
+    method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+    kernel = method.moe_kernel
+    assert kernel is not None
+    assert isinstance(kernel.fused_experts, MuseSparkAiterW4A16Experts)
+

+    topk_logits, topk_ids = torch.topk(
+        torch.randn(num_tokens, num_experts, device=device), top_k, dim=-1
+    )
+    topk_weights = torch.softmax(topk_logits, dim=-1)

+        return kernel.apply(
+            hidden_states,
+            triton_weight(layer, "w13_weight"),
+            triton_weight(layer, "w2_weight"),
+            topk_weights,
+            topk_ids,

+            global_num_experts=num_experts,
+            expert_map=None,
+            apply_router_weight_on_input=False,
+        )
+
+    actual = _run().clone()
+    routes = _reference_route_outputs(hidden_states, w13_ref, w2_ref, topk_ids)
+    expected = (
+        (_rms_norm(routes, out_dtype=torch.float32) * topk_weights[..., None])
+        .sum(dim=1)
+        .to(dtype)
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        captured = _run()
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(captured, actual, rtol=0, atol=0)

+class MuseSparkAiterW4A16Experts(_RouteOutputHandoff, mk.FusedMoEExpertsModular):
+    """gfx942 MXFP4 experts: AITER Triton W4A16, one unweighted output per route.

+    Keeps the checkpoint's MXFP4 weights and runs BF16 activations. Each
+    (token, route) pair is expanded to its own row and routed top-1 to its
+    expert with a unit gate, so GEMM2 writes the unweighted per-route output
+    that the MuseSpark post-expert norm consumes.

+
+    def __init__(
+        self,

+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(moe_config, quant_config)
+        if not isinstance(quant_config, MuseSparkQuarkOCPMXMoEQuantConfig):
+            raise TypeError(

+            )

+            raise ValueError("MuseSpark1x post-expert norm is not configured.")

+
+        if getattr(routing, "_USE_HERD", False):

+                "and are incompatible with AITER_TRITON_USE_HERD."
+            )

+    def expects_unquantized_inputs(self) -> bool:

+    @staticmethod

+        return activation == MoEActivation.SILU
+

+        return not moe_parallel_config.use_ep and moe_parallel_config.dp_size == 1

+        expert_tokens_meta: mk.ExpertTokensMetadata | None,
+        activation: MoEActivation,
+    ) -> tuple[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]]:

+    def apply(
+        self,
+        output: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        w1: torch.Tensor,
+        w2: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_weights: torch.Tensor,
+        topk_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        activation: MoEActivation,
+        global_num_experts: int,
+        expert_map: torch.Tensor | None,
+        a1q_scale: torch.Tensor | None,
+        a2_scale: torch.Tensor | None,
+        workspace13: torch.Tensor,

+        if expert_map is not None:
+            raise NotImplementedError(

+            )

+        num_tokens, top_k = topk_ids.shape
+        hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape[-1]
+        num_routes = num_tokens * top_k
+        expanded_hidden_states = take_expanded(hidden_states, top_k)
+        if expanded_hidden_states is None:
+            expanded_hidden_states = hidden_states.repeat_interleave(top_k, dim=0)
+
+        # One-hot logits route each expanded row to exactly its own expert, and
+        # the top-1 softmax gate is exactly 1, so GEMM2's output stays unweighted.
+        route_logits = torch.zeros(
+            (num_routes, global_num_experts),
+            dtype=expanded_hidden_states.dtype,
+            device=expanded_hidden_states.device,
+        )
+        route_logits.scatter_(1, topk_ids.reshape(num_routes, 1).long(), 1.0)

+            hidden_states=expanded_hidden_states,
+            w1=w1,
+            w2=w2,
+            gating_output=route_logits,
+            topk=1,

+        assert quant_config.post_expert_norm_fn is not None

+            quant_config.post_expert_norm_fn,
+            pre_norm_all_reduce=self.moe_config.moe_parallel_config.tp_size > 1,
+            take_route_output=self._take_route_output,
+        )
